name: Oman
summary: A vertical red band at the hoist with the national emblem of a khanjar dagger over crossed swords, beside white, red and green horizontal bands. It was introduced in 1970 by Sultan Qaboos bin Said.
origin: Oman historically used plain red flags. Sultan Qaboos introduced the current design on 17 December 1970, shortly after taking power, adding white and green.
In 1995 the proportions were changed and the white and green bands made equal in width to the red.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The battles against invaders; the traditional colour of Omani flags.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: Peace and prosperity; also the Imam, the religious leader.

colors.name: Green
colors.meaning: Fertility, the Jebel Akhdar (Green Mountain) and Islam.

symbols.name: Khanjar and swords
symbols.description: A traditional curved dagger in its sheath over two crossed swords, joined by a belt.
symbols.meaning: The national emblem of the Al Said dynasty, adopted in the 18th century.

facts: The khanjar is still worn on formal occasions by Omani men.
The emblem also appears on Omani banknotes.
Sultan Qaboos ruled from 1970 until his death in 2020.
clues: A red hoist band with a dagger over crossed swords, beside white, red and green bands.
Its emblem shows a traditional curved dagger.
Introduced in 1970 by a sultan who ruled for fifty years.
